canonical.title: Find Eventual Safe States
canonical.sourceFilePath: 13. Graphs/3. Topo Sort Problems/05. Find Eventual Safe State.cpp

narrative.title: Certifying the Runaway-Free Junctions
narrative.scenario: A rail dispatcher's one-way junction map must certify which starting junctions are safe: from them, every train, however it chooses its route, eventually rolls into an end-of-line terminal and stops. Junctions that can feed an endless loop — directly or one hop removed — can never be certified, and the dispatcher lists only the safe ones in ascending order.
narrative.inputFormat: A directed graph as an adjacency list graph where graph[i] lists the junctions node i points to.
narrative.outputFormat: Return every safe node in ascending order.

testCases.explanation: Nodes 2, 4 and 6 roll straight into terminal 5; node 0, 1 or 3 can drift into the 0-1-3 loop.
Node 0 is itself terminal; 1 and 2 chase each other forever.

hintLevels: Level 1: Safe means 'cannot reach any cycle' — terminals are safe by definition and safety flows backwards.
Level 2: Reverse every edge and peel terminals like Kahn's, but on outdegree; survivors of the peel are cycle-tainted.
Level 3: Nodes released by the reverse topological drain, sorted ascending, are exactly the safe set.
